transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… mostly sleep. It’s kind of fallen apart lately. I’ll be in bed for hours, laptop closed, but I’m still going over work deadlines and payments and class stuff in my head. And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really shut off.
Do you find yourself worrying about these things during the day as well, not just when you're trying to sleep?

Yeah… it’s during the day too. My mind kind of jumps around—from work, to whether school is a waste of money, to what my family might think if I can’t keep up. Even small things start feeling like they could mess everything up.
Do you ever find yourself avoiding certain tasks or situations because of these worries?

Yeah… I guess so. I’ve been putting things off, especially work stuff and my certificate classes, and now I’m missing deadlines and falling behind. And I’ve kind of stopped doing the things that used to help me stay steady, like yoga or running… even cooking.
Have you experienced any episodes where you suddenly felt intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I don’t think so… not like suddenly out of nowhere and peaking fast. It’s more like I’m tense for a long time.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?
I’m not really sure… I guess I do feel keyed up sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it restless exactly.
Do you avoid social situations because you worry about what others might think of you?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I mean, I think about what people think sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I avoid social situations because of it.
Has something very stressful or traumatic happened to you recently or in the past?
Not really… nothing I’d call traumatic. I mean, stressful things happen, but nothing specific like that comes to mind.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?
Not that I’ve really noticed. I don’t weigh myself much, but my clothes seem about the same.
Has there been any significant change or event in your life that you think might be contributing to your current state?
Maybe… I think it started when I began an evening graduate certificate program, while still working full-time as an analyst. That was about a year and three months ago. I guess it’s been a lot.
Do you think your worries and stress are overwhelmingly about the specific challenges of managing work and your graduate certificate program?

Mostly, but it doesn’t stay just there. My mind jumps around… like if I’m behind at work, or if school is a waste of money, or if my family thinks I can’t handle it. Even small things start feeling like they could mess up everything.
Is there something specific about the graduate certificate program or your work that you think triggered these worries and stress?
I think it was really when I started the evening program on top of my full-time analyst job. It’s been… about a year and three months now. That’s when it seemed to start.
Do you think your worries would decrease significantly if you were able to manage your work and graduate certificate program responsibilities more effectively?

Maybe somewhat, but… I don’t think it would fully go away. My mind keeps jumping from one thing to another — work, whether school is worth the money, whether my family thinks I can’t handle it. Even little problems start feeling like they could mess everything up.
Do you think your worries and stress would stop if the sources of stress, like your work and graduate program, were completely resolved?

No… I don’t think it would just stop. Even if work and school were fixed, my mind would probably find something else. It jumps from being behind, to wasting money, to what my family thinks… and then some small thing starts feeling like it could ruin everything.
Do you think your worries and stress are directly related to the challenges of managing your work and graduate program, or are they more about a wide range of everyday things in general?

More the second one, I think. It’s not just work and school. My mind kind of jumps around — like if I’m falling behind at work, or wasting money on the program, or if my family thinks I can’t handle things. And then even small issues feel like they could mess up everything.
Do you think your worries started as a direct response to taking on the graduate certificate program and the increased workload?
Yeah… I guess it did start around then. It’s been about a year and three months, since I started the evening certificate program while still working full-time.
Have you been worrying about these everyday things for more than six months?
Yeah… definitely more than six months. It’s been about a year and three months, since I started the evening program while still working full-time.
Do you think your worries and stress would be significantly better if you could just stop thinking about them for a while?

I mean… I try to do that, to just stop thinking and focus on one thing. But it doesn’t really work. One worry turns into another, and then I’m checking my calendar or my budget or assignments again and again instead of actually doing anything.
Do you think your worries and stress are primarily about one specific issue or are they spread across many different areas of your life?
It’s… not just one thing. It kind of jumps around. Work, school, money, what my family thinks. Even small stuff starts feeling like it could mess everything up.
Do you think your worries and stress would disappear if you were able to find a way to cope with or resolve the issues related to your work and graduate program?

Not really. I think even if work or school got sorted out, my mind would probably just move to something else… money, my family thinking I can’t handle things. It’s like every little problem starts feeling like it could ruin everything.
Do you think your worries and stress are more related to your own internal expectations and fears or to the external pressures and stressors from your work and graduate program?

Probably both, but… it feels like it’s coming from inside my own head more. Like, I’ll start with work, then I’m worrying I’m wasting money on school, then what my family will think if I can’t keep up. Even small things start feeling like they could mess up my whole future.
